title: Invocation Orchestrator: schema locator, sanitization & validation runbook
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Goal: define a pragmatic, runtime-friendly JSON schema format and validation lifecycle for tool/function invocations. This ticket produces a runbook and implementation guidance for: 1) how the platform locates and loads a call schema for a model-invoked tool; 2) canonicalization/sanitization rules applied prior to validation; 3) three validation modes (strict/coerce/warn) and associated developer UX; 4) an error catalog mapping machine codes to user-facing messages and telemetry tags; 5) compatibility shims for legacy SDK shapes and incremental rollout strategy.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook doc produced and reviewed by Runtime and SDK leads
Prototype validator implemented in the runtime that supports strict/coerce/warn modes
Backward-compatibility adapter for legacy param shapes with at least two heuristic rules documented
Error catalog published and integrated with Console error grouping (error-code + reason + remediation)
Telemetry events emitted for validation failures containing error_code, schema_id, validation_mode, and sample_hash
runtime_behavior: On incoming tool invocation the runtime will: 1) resolve schema: check request metadata for schema_id, then model-discovered tools catalog, then fall back to schema registry lookup by tool signature; 2) perform canonicalization (trim strings, normalize numeric types, expand legacy aliases) depending on validation_mode; 3) run schema validation producing either success, corrected_payload (if coerce), or error; 4) attach validation outcome and error_code to the request trace and routing metadata; 5) when configured, attempt an automated retry with coerce rules applied before returning an error to the caller.
validation_modes: strict - reject on any schema violation with deterministic error_code and no mutation
coerce - attempt well-defined coercions (string->number, parse ISO timestamps, normalize booleans) and return warnings when coercions applied
warn - accept payloads but emit validation warnings and sampling telemetry for soft failures
error_catalog: INVOCATION_MISSING_REQUIRED - required parameter missing; message: 'Required parameter {param} is missing. See schema {schema_id}.'; remediation: provide the missing parameter
INVOCATION_TYPE_MISMATCH - parameter {param} expected {expected_type} but received {got_type}; remediation: coerce if mode=coerce or fix caller input
INVOCATION_FORMAT_INVALID - value for {param} failed format check (e.g., date-time, uri); remediation: validate against format or use different field
INVOCATION_EXTRA_PROPERTIES - additional unexpected fields detected; remediation: remove unknown keys or set validation mode to warn/coerce
INVOCATION_ENUM_MISMATCH - value not in allowed set; remediation: map to nearest allowed value or return guidance
INVOCATION_COERCION_FAILURE - attempted coercion failed; remediation: inspect sample in console and suggest corrective action
INVOCATION_SCHEMA_NOT_FOUND - no schema could be resolved for this tool signature; remediation: register schema or include schema_id in request
migration_plan: Phase 1: implement validator and warn mode, collect telemetry for 2 weeks. Phase 2: enable coerce mode as opt-in for SDKs and hosted customers; publish SDK flags. Phase 3: flip default to strict for new schemas, keep warn for legacy. Phase 4: offer configurable per-tenant policies and Console UI to view sampled failing invocations and suggested schema updates.
telemetry: Emit structured events on validation outcome: {event:invocation.validation, schema_id, validation_mode, error_code (or OK), sample_id (hashed), model_version, route_id}. Ensure events are sampled (1% by default) for soft failures and unsampled for P0 errors. Expose aggregated metrics in Console: validation_failure_rate, coercion_rate, avg_coercions_per_invocation.
qa_tests: unit tests for canonicalizers (trim, normalize boolean variants, numeric parsing)
end-to-end test invoking the runtime with strict/coerce/warn payloads using the test schema registry
fuzz test sending randomly shaped payloads to assert no uncaught exceptions
integration test asserting telemetry fields are emitted and visible in dev Console
roll_out_steps: Canary deploy validator in dev cluster with warn mode (2 nodes)
Collect telemetry and iterate on human-friendly messages
Expose coerce flag to SDKs and sample a small percentage of production traffic
Announce default policy change and update docs and SDK changelogs
notes: Keep schema authoring ergonomics simple: prefer small, focused schemas over giant monoliths
Avoid silent destructive coercions (e.g., truncating arrays) — only allow lossy coercions with explicit schema opt-in
Console should show example remediations for top 10 error codes automatically
